newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares slip on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares slip on speculative selling.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index lost early gains and ended down slightly on Thursday due to speculative selling, brokers said.

The B share index dipped 0.76 points, or 0.85 percent, to 88.59 on turnover of HK$13.74 million, compared with Wednesday's HK$12.88 million. Brokers said the market would remain sluggish for a period.

"Institutions have little interest in such a boring market, which has been dominated by limited speculative trading for a long time," one analyst said. "Some changes may take place after companies release their 1996 results."
Shenzhen Petrochemical, the biggest loser, fell HK$0.48, or 17.39 percent, to HK$2.28 in thin trade of 3,524 shares due to speculative selling, brokers said.

Television maker Konka followed suit, sliding HK$0.50 to HK$6.00, with only 350 shares changing hands. Newcomer Changan had the day's heaviest volume of 2.97 million shares to end up HK$0.04 at HK$1.74, well below its offer price of HK$1.89 per share.
China Merchants put in the best performance, up HK$0.11 to HK$3.37, with 197,100 shares traded. Dadonghai, the second most active counter, rose HK$0.02 to HK$1.32 on volume of 540,300 shares.

The A share index gained 9.22 points, or 2.24 percent, to close at a record high of 421.03 as turnover rose to 16.27 billion yuan from 14.17 billion the previous session. The composite index rose 8.18 points, or 2.14 percent, to 390.53.
Brokers said the A share market is being buoyed by a steady inflow of fresh money, triggered in part by the A share index's strong gains since Monday.
The A index has repeatedly hit record highs this week and a slight correction is expected, they said.
Air-conditioner maker Guangdong Meide soared 1.79 yuan, or 17.24 percent, to 12.17 yuan in heavy trade of 39.99 million shares due to institutional speculative demand.
Market leader Shenzhen Development Bank jumped 0.69 yuan to 18.29 yuan, with volume reaching 50.96 million shares, which boosted market sentiment, brokers said.
